summary: SL-039 closed the one missing PS-002 criterion (C4, results fill in as the scan goes) with a scanner-thread TopLevelTracker. It publishes immutable snapshots of the scan root's direct children on ScanProgress and ScanResult, and the window shows them in a virtualized ListBox. It deliberately avoided both no-go spikes, which were about a second thread reading the live ScanStore. It shipped with no lap after design: 170/170 Core tests, 18 window cases, scan time -0.5% against trunk, and real-data validation on C:\Windows and C:\ProgramData. It rests on an unanswered scope question (does a one-level list satisfy 'results fill in'?), a 'Done' state that real hardlinks make non-final, and a network pass nobody has run for two slices.

payload.summary: SL-039 closed the one missing PS-002 criterion (C4, results fill in as the scan goes) with a scanner-thread TopLevelTracker. It publishes immutable snapshots of the scan root's direct children on ScanProgress and ScanResult, and the window shows them in a virtualized ListBox. It deliberately avoided both no-go spikes, which were about a second thread reading the live ScanStore. It shipped with no lap after design: 170/170 Core tests, 18 window cases, scan time -0.5% against trunk, and real-data validation on C:\Windows and C:\ProgramData. It rests on an unanswered scope question (does a one-level list satisfy 'results fill in'?), a 'Done' state that real hardlinks make non-final, and a network pass nobody has run for two slices.
payload.estimate_error: Size and tier were about right. Medium/medium covered 11 source files touching the counting-critical scanner, 15 new Core tests, 3 new window cases and one named-only measurement, with no lap after design and a measured -0.5% scan cost. The error is that the uncertainty that mattered was scope, and the sizing did not carry it. The build-check said that if 'results' only means the running counters, the slice was already built. The design assumed a one-level list closes C4, and a drill-down tree would have been a far larger slice with both spike prerequisites. A single designer and nobody arguing meant that scope was never contested, and the question is still unanswered at commit. The design was also under-sized on contact: the only proposal was written without opening Scanner.cs or ScanStore.cs, and its central 'credit on every exit' amendment was wrong. Sizing critique-review out was defensible only because the disposition step read the code and corrected the critic. It did not cover M2, which was accepted without a reason and turned out impossible.
what_went_wrong: The design and critique reasoned about Scanner.cs without reading it. The design's own coherence_check says the hook points were 'NOT verified here'. Its key decision 'credit on every exit from a listing, including an interrupted one' rested on partial adds that do not exist, because an aborted listing returns at Scanner.cs:139 before anything is appended. The critique then built M1's cancelled-folder risk, M4 part 1 and m2 (partial root listing) on the same premise. Three of 12 findings were overridden (m2, m3, m6) and several more were narrowed (M1, M4, m4, m8). The disposition step and the O-001 discharge fixed it. The builder never built the amendment.

The critique's M2 fix ('once Done, figures never change in later snapshots') contradicts the design's own tracker.Moved, which moves a hardlink's in-place correction into an earlier row that may already be Done. It was accepted-pending with no reason, the builder found it impossible (declared as a deviation), and validate then saw it on real data: one C:\Windows row changed bytes after it was Done, and 47,409 later hardlink names sat in a different row from the name that was charged. The window shows no suffix for a Done row, so 'Done' still implies a finality the data cannot keep. Nobody has decided what to do about it.

The scope question ('is a one-level list enough to close PS-002?') was raised at design, carried by the build, and reported 'not reached' by validate. Three stages listed it and none could answer it. The slice closes PS-002's C4 on an assumption.

The design put the results list inside ScanningPanel, which collapses at every ending, while also requiring the ending to show the final snapshot. The builder found the contradiction and moved the list to its own panel. The critique read the design against MainWindow.xaml and did not.

The O-001 discharge, which told the build to drop the design's central 'credit on every exit' amendment and that credits follow the stack, reached the builder clipped at 220 characters ('Credits follow the st...'). The builder had to infer the rest from the critique dispositions.

The halts, not re-runs, account for the 'ran twice' count on build-check, risk-spike, design and critique. index.json shows one attempt per stage, so the rework tally overstates rework. The real friction was elsewhere: the tool safety filter refused three commands across the survey and validate (a Remove-Item on a '\b' path pattern; a probe file with a variable named rd and // comments; a watch run that removed Env: variables next to the C:\Windows root), and each cost a rerun. The build also needed four passes on TopLevelTests before 15/15 (missing parent folders, a sparse-file folder, a wrong 'stoppedInBig' condition), plus a CS1593 compile error and a void hook measurement (containers counted before layout).

The network pass (N-001..N-004, StalledShareTests) has now been owed across two consecutive slices, SL-038 and SL-039. Nobody has measured Cancel or the results list on a stalled share, and this slice changed the scanner listing path and the window again. No stage could run it, because it changes SMB mappings.

missed.what: The critique's M2 fix required 'once a row is Done/Unreadable/NotFollowed, its figures are identical in every later snapshot'. It never checked that against the design's own tracker.Moved, which by design credits a hardlink's later in-place size correction to an earlier row that may already be Done. A check that would have caught it: for every 'invariant holds once state S' fix, grep the design for any operation that can mutate the object after S. The fix was accepted-pending with no reason recorded.
missed.caught_by: build (declared as a deviation: the invariant cannot hold as stated), then validate on real C:\Windows data, where one row changed bytes after Done. The UI consequence is still undecided.

missed.what: The critique did not ask what Scanner.cs does with a listing aborted by cancel. The abort returns at Scanner.cs:139 before AddEntry, and the root is read whole into DirectoryReader before any append, so an interrupted listing commits nothing. It endorsed the design's 'credit on every exit including interrupted' and filed M1 (cancelled folder counted as unreadable), M4 part 1 (in-flight cancel with partial adds) and m2 (partial root listing) against a path that does not exist.
missed.caught_by: the critique's own model disposition step (M4 'because', m2 overridden) and the O-001 discharge, before build

missed.what: The design placed the results list under CountersText inside ScanningPanel, but ScanningPanel collapses at every ending, while the same design requires the ending handler to always show the final snapshot with a 'what was read before the stop' header. The critique did not read the design's layout against MainWindow.xaml's panel visibility.
missed.caught_by: build (declared deviation: the list moved to its own panel below the scanning and outcome panels)

learned.lesson: For any slice that edits Scanner.cs, give the designer and the critic the scanner's control flow, not just line citations. The survey cited Scanner.cs:60/:139/:163/:165 without describing what an aborted listing does. Three findings and one key design decision were built on a wrong guess.
learned.evidence: The design's coherence_check lists 'Scanner.cs gives a place to credit interrupted listings' as NOT verified. m2, m6 and M4's 'why' were overridden or corrected from the code. The O-001 discharge reversed the design's central amendment.

learned.lesson: Scanner facts the next scanner-touching slice can rely on: FolderDone (Scanner.cs:137-166) is the single exit for every non-root folder and records unreadable folders itself (:149-152). An aborted listing commits nothing (:139, before any append). The root listing is read whole before any append. There is no separate long-path listing branch, because everything goes through LongPath.Child and FolderDone. Run.Finish (~:275-294) is the only place a ScanResult is built. MainWindow creates a new ScanProgress per scan (MainWindow.xaml.cs:135). The per-listing publish is at :163. The stack tuple _pending (:62-64) can carry per-folder data (the top-row index) at O(1).
learned.evidence: The disposition 'because' texts for M1, m1, m2, m4, m5 and m6, and the code review's line citations (Scanner.cs:64, :139, :144-145, :166, :171-174, :285, :292-294).

learned.lesson: 'Done' is not final in this app. Hardlinks are charged to the first name, and the second name's probe corrects the first record in place (CorrectSizes, which the tracker relays via Moved), so a per-folder total can change after the folder finished. This is common on system trees, not an edge. Any next slice that shows or sorts per-folder totals (tree, shares, treemap) must not treat a finished folder's figure as stable, and must not add a test asserting it.
learned.evidence: Builder deviation M2. Validate on C:\Windows: 47,409 later hardlink names in a different row from the charged name, and one row changed bytes after Done. The window shows no suffix for Done.

learned.lesson: The snapshot-on-the-progress-channel pattern is proven for this codebase: the scanner thread owns mutable accumulators, publishes immutable snapshots (constructor copies rows behind Array.AsReadOnly) by Volatile.Write, and the window compares by ReferenceEquals. It avoided both no-go spikes and cost -0.5% scan time (410.2 vs 408.1 ms median on a 196,583-entry tree; flat 100k-folder root about 7.0 s either way). The tree slice can extend it. Doing the two 'needs first' items instead (store published before Finish with an ordered child-range publish, and a consistent rollup read path) means deleting the fitness rule 'the window never touches the scan store' on purpose.
learned.evidence: Spike verdicts (12-18% at 200k, 28% at 5M, child>parent in 20/20 runs). Build benchmark. All 28 fitness rules hold with the narrowed store rule '(?<!\bresult)\.Store\b'.

learned.lesson: Measured baselines for the next window slice: the ListBox at 100,000 rows with a two-TextBlock row and virtualization on gave refresh p95 25.4-46.5 ms (max 64.3) and Input-probe p95 8.2-15.7 ms across 4 runs, with 5-6 realized containers. The spike's limits are 100 ms and 200 ms. M-001 takes about 35 s, is timing on a shared PC, and stays named-only. A heavier row template needs re-measuring. The spike also failed twice on a busy PC (about 94% machine CPU), so the refresh must stay droppable.
learned.evidence: M-001 build runs, code-review re-run (refresh p95 25.8 ms, Input p95 11.8 ms), validate re-run, and spike 2's constraints list.

learned.lesson: Treat a critique disposition with 'because: null' as a fix nobody checked against the code, and check it first at build. 2 of the 9 accepted-pending dispositions (M2 and m7) carried no reason, and M2 was the one that turned out impossible. With critique-review sized out, the disposition step was the only reader of the code, so an unreasoned disposition means no reader.
learned.evidence: M2 and m7 dispositions have because: null. The M2 deviation at build. The critique-review stage record: 'does not get its review reviewed'.

learned.lesson: The network pass is a standing debt, not a per-slice item. It is a person's run because it changes SMB mappings, and it goes stale whenever a slice touches MainWindow*, Scanning/**, tests/window/FsaWindowHook/** or WindowCases.ps1. SL-038 already owed it and SL-039 renewed it. A next slice touching those files must state that Cancel on a stalled share (SL-020 recorded a 62-66 s wait with a 'Still waiting' line from 2 s) is unmeasured, not claim cancel-safety.
learned.evidence: Build and validate both list 'not reached: Network pass'. The survey says SL-038's docs say a person owes that run.

learned.lesson: The shipped exe carries no test seam, so a window case cannot make Scanner.Scan throw. Any slice whose criterion includes 'the window clears on a scan fault' needs a seam-free way designed at the start (the startup hook is the only injection route), or it stays unverified. The hook already has watch and measure modes and FSA_HOOK_SLOW_REFRESH_MS. Reuse them rather than adding modes, and note that the hook is built by Update-Hook outside FsAnalyser.slnx.
learned.evidence: Build and validate 'not reached' on the C-010 throw sub-shape. In report mode the UI fault exits 70 with no report (C-012). The code reviewer confirmed only that sub-shape of case 10 was not fed.

learned.lesson: The engine clips an obligation's discharge text to 220 characters before the build reads it, and the clipped part can be the instruction that reverses the design. Until that is fixed, a builder facing a discharged 'decide' obligation must read the critique dispositions and the discharge record in full, not the summary line.
learned.evidence: O-001's discharge reached the build as 'Credits follow the st...'. The builder inferred the rest and deviated correctly, but only because the dispositions carried the reasoning.

candidates.title: Person runs the opt-in network pass: WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork, then Core.Tests filtered to Network=SMB-LOOPBACK
candidates.why: Stale since SL-038 and made stale again by SL-039, which changed the scanner listing path, MainWindow, the hook and WindowCases.ps1. Cancel and the new results list on a stalled share are unmeasured, and SL-020 recorded a 62-66 s wait there. Every further slice on these files widens the unmeasured change.

candidates.title: Decide what a Done row promises when a hardlink correction lands later, and show it or stop implying finality
candidates.why: Validate saw a Done row change bytes on real C:\Windows, with 47,409 later hardlink names in a different row from the charged one. The window prints no suffix for Done. The critique's M2 'Done is immutable' fix was impossible and is a still-open person decision.

candidates.title: Folder tree: expand a top-level row while the scan runs (store published before Finish with ordered child-range publish, plus a consistent rollup read path)
candidates.why: The design and both no-go spikes name these as the 'needs first' items for any drill-down, and the design note assigns them to a later tree slice. SL-039 delivered only a one-level list, and whether that closes PS-002 is still unanswered. The fitness rule 'the window never touches the scan store' would be deleted on purpose there.

candidates.title: Run the shipped exe on a whole real drive with a cold cache and record memory, refresh and Cancel latency
candidates.why: PS-002 speaks of a big drive. The largest real scans were C:\Windows (346,873 entries, first run 15.6 s cold, then 7-10 s warm) and C:\ProgramData (257,972). Nothing at millions of entries went through the tracker and list. M-001 covers only 100,000 synthetic top-level rows. Validate lists both cold-cache and whole-drive as not reached.

candidates.title: Add a standing EndingObeysSkip mutant for L-002 to tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1
candidates.why: The build showed L-002 fails against a mutant whose ending obeys the skip rule (topLevel.final False, reading 1, bytes 393216 vs 524288), but only by hand. Nothing in the suite proves the guard that keeps a stale 'reading' row off the screen keeps biting.

candidates.title: Engine: stop clipping obligation discharge text at 220 characters where the build reads it
candidates.why: O-001's discharge, which reversed the design's central amendment, reached the builder as 'Credits follow the st...'. The builder had to infer the decision from the critique dispositions. This is the evidence-that-never-crosses shape again, on a decision the build acted on.

candidates.title: Give the hook a seam-free way to make Scanner.Scan fault after rows are shown, so C-010's clear-on-fault case can be checked at window level
candidates.why: Build and validate both left 'the list clears when the scan faults after rows were shown' unverified. The shipped exe cannot fault the scan without violating 'the shipped app carries no test seam', and the clearing code is checked only indirectly through L-003's shared endings.

candidates.title: Publish progress inside a very large single-folder listing, not only once per listing (Scanner.cs:163)
candidates.why: The survey measured a flat 6,000-folder tree jumping 0 to 6,000 folders in one publish. Rows are seeded from the root listing, but a huge folder anywhere shows no movement until its listing returns. This limits how well the watch behaviour PS-002 asks for holds on a big drive.

unknowns: How large are the post-Done byte shifts on hardlink-heavy real trees (C:\Windows/WinSxS) once the app is used for real, and are they big enough that a person would read a re-sorting or growing Done row as a bug?
What does Cancel cost on a stalled share now that FolderExited and the row credit sit in the listing path? SL-020 recorded a 62-66 s wait, and no stage has re-measured it for this slice.

Does the per-listing publish plus 250 ms timer give a usable watch experience on a whole cold-cache drive with millions of entries and a few huge folders? The largest real scan was 346,873 entries, warm.
